title: Regular Polygons Assessment
description: Show that you can classify regular and irregular polygons using side and angle measurements.

questions.question: A polygon has 8 sides. What additional information is needed to prove it is a regular octagon?
options: All sides are straight.
All sides are equal and all interior angles are equal.
It has more than 4 sides.
It has at least two equal angles.
questions.explanation: An octagon has 8 sides, but it is regular only if all sides and all interior angles are equal.

questions.question: A triangle has angle measures 60°, 60°, and 60°. Its sides are 4 cm, 4 cm, and 4 cm. Which classification is correct?
options: Regular triangle
Irregular triangle
Regular quadrilateral
Irregular pentagon
questions.explanation: The figure is a triangle, and all its sides and angles are equal, so it is regular.

questions.question: A quadrilateral has side lengths 6 cm, 6 cm, 6 cm, and 6 cm. Its angle measures are 90°, 90°, 90°, and 90°. Which statement is true?
options: It is regular because both side and angle tests pass.
It is irregular because quadrilaterals cannot be regular.
It is irregular because all angles are right angles.
There is not enough information to classify it.
questions.explanation: A square is a regular quadrilateral because all four sides and all four angles are equal.

questions.question: A pentagon has side lengths 3 cm, 3 cm, 3 cm, 3 cm, and 4 cm. Its angle measures are all 108°. Why is it irregular?
options: It has too many equal angles.
It has exactly 5 sides.
Not all side lengths are equal.
A pentagon can never be regular.
questions.explanation: The side lengths must all be equal. The 4 cm side makes the pentagon irregular.

questions.question: If all sides of a polygon are equal, then the polygon is always regular.
questions.explanation: A regular polygon must also have all interior angles equal. Equal sides alone do not guarantee regularity.

questions.question: A regular decagon has 10 sides, all equal in length, and 10 equal interior angles.
questions.explanation: A decagon has 10 sides, and regular means all sides and all interior angles are equal.

questions.question: A regular polygon with 6 sides is called a regular ______.
questions.explanation: A 6-sided polygon is a hexagon, so a regular 6-sided polygon is a regular hexagon.

questions.question: A student says, "This octagon looks regular, so I do not need to measure it." What is the best response?
options: Correct, appearance is always enough.
Correct, all octagons are regular.
Incorrect, regularity should be checked with side and angle measurements.
Incorrect, octagons cannot be measured.
questions.explanation: A shape may look regular but still have unequal sides or angles. Measurements give better evidence.

questions.question: A 5-sided polygon has all side lengths equal to 7 cm. Its angle measures are 100°, 110°, 105°, 115°, and 110°. Classify it and justify your answer.
questions.correctAnswer: It is an irregular pentagon. It has 5 sides and equal side lengths, but the interior angles are not all equal.
questions.explanation: The polygon is a pentagon because it has 5 sides. It is irregular because regular polygons need equal sides and equal angles.

questions.question: Explain the two measurements you should compare before identifying a polygon as regular.
questions.correctAnswer: Compare all side lengths and all interior angle measures. The polygon is regular only if every side length matches and every interior angle measure matches.
questions.explanation: Regularity requires two kinds of evidence: equal sides and equal interior angles.
